items.prompt: Which word has two meanings: a flying animal and a piece of sports equipment?

options.why: A ball is used in sport, but it is not an animal.
A net is sports equipment, but it is not an animal.
An owl flies, but it is not sports equipment.

hints: A word with two meanings and one spelling is a homonym.
Think of an animal that flies at night.
Then think of something used to hit a ball. Do they share a name?
items.explanation: Bat is a homonym. It can mean a flying animal or the piece of equipment used in sports such as cricket.

items.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?

options.why: After a vowel, the shul ending is usually spelt -cial.
This spells the sound, but not the correct letters.
The i and the a are in the wrong order.

hints: Say the word slowly: spe-shul.
After a vowel, the shul ending is usually spelt -cial, as in official.
Write spe, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Special ends in -cial, like official and social. The -cial ending usually follows a vowel.

items.prompt: Match each sentence to the meaning of the word in it.
pairs: Wind the string around the stick.
A tear rolled down her cheek.
a drop of water from the eye
to save sound to play later
hints: Each pair of sentences uses the same spelling with a different meaning.
Say each sentence aloud. The word may sound different too.
Start with the wind. Is it moving air or turning something?
items.explanation: Wind, tear and record are homographs: they are spelt the same but have different meanings, and they are often pronounced differently.

items.prompt: In which sentence does bank mean the side of a river?

options.text: Mum put the money in the bank.
options.why: Here bank means a place that keeps money.

options.text: We had a picnic on the bank of the Brantas River.
You can bank on me to help.
options.why: Here bank on means rely on.

options.text: The plane began to bank to the left.
options.why: Here bank means tilt to one side while turning.

hints: Bank is a homonym with several meanings.
Look for clue words near bank in each sentence.
Read the words that come straight after bank.
items.explanation: In the picnic sentence, the clue river shows that bank means the land along the side of the water.

items.prompt: Write the full words using -cial or -tial. The par___ eclipse lasted an hour. Here is the offi___ timetable.
hints: Listen for the letter just before the shul sound.
-tial usually follows a consonant, and -cial usually follows a vowel.
Look at the last letter before the gap in each word.
items.explanation: Partial has r before the ending, so it takes -tial. Official has i before the ending, so it takes -cial.

items.prompt: Which sentence is spelt correctly?

options.why: Confident ends in -ent, so the noun ends in -ence.
The ending is spelt -ence, with a c.
The second vowel is i: con-fi-dence.

hints: Think of the adjective: confident.
If an adjective ends in -ent, the noun usually ends in -ence.
Write confident, then change the last letters.
items.explanation: Confident becomes confidence. Adjectives ending in -ent usually make nouns ending in -ence, like patient and patience.

items.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?

options.why: Words ending in -ible change to -ibly.
The root is horrible, so the ending is -ibly.
The -le changes to -ly. You do not keep the e.

hints: The root word is horrible.
Words ending in -le change the -le to -ly.
Write horrible, then change its last two letters.
items.explanation: Horrible ends in -le, so the -le changes to -ly: horribly, like sensibly and gently.

items.prompt: Add -ed to each verb. prefer: ___ visit: ___
hints: Say each verb and listen for which syllable is stressed.
If the last syllable is stressed and ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant.
Say pre-FER and VIS-it. Which one is stressed at the end?
items.explanation: Prefer is stressed at the end, so the r doubles: preferred. Visit is stressed at the start, so the t does not double: visited.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that are spelt correctly.

options.why: Occur is stressed at the end, so the r doubles: occurred.
Refer is stressed at the end, so the r doubles: referred.
Garden is stressed at the start, so the n does not double: gardening.

hints: Look carefully at the double letters.
When a word is stressed on its last syllable, the final consonant usually doubles before -ed or -ing.
Say each root word and clap the syllables. Where is the stress?
items.explanation: Travelled (the British spelling), beginning and forgotten are correct. The others should be occurred, referred and gardening.

items.prompt: Which word fits all three gaps? We can ___ the car here. The ___ has a big pond. Let’s play in the ___ after school.

options.why: Leave fits the first gap only.
Garden fits the last two gaps, but you cannot garden a car.
Stop fits the first gap only.

hints: The word is a homonym with more than one meaning.
Test each option in all three gaps.
Start with the first gap: what can you do with a car?
items.explanation: Park is a homonym. It means to leave a car somewhere, and it also means a public garden with a pond or a playground.

items.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? I would like a ___ of cake.
hints: Think about what you cut from a cake.
Piece begins like pie.
A piece of pie.
items.explanation: Piece means a part of something. Peace means calm.

options.why: Peace means calm and quiet. It sounds the same but has a different meaning.
Piece has an i and an e. Something is missing.
In piece the i comes before the e.

items.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? The ___ is sunny today.
hints: Think about rain, wind and sun.
The word begins with the letters w, e, a.
We, ather.
items.explanation: Weather is the state of the air and sky. Whether means if.

options.why: Whether means if. It sounds the same but does not fit.
The letters are in the wrong order. Weather ends in -ther.
This word is misspelt. There is no h after the first e.

items.prompt: ___ going to the market, and ___ bags are over ___.
hints: They’re is a short form of two words.
Their shows that something belongs to them. There shows a place.
Say the first gap as they are.
items.explanation: They’re means they are, their shows ownership and there points to a place.

items.prompt: Listen and spell the word.
hints: It has one collar and two sleeves.
Remember: one c and two s.
Neces, sary.
items.explanation: Necessary has one c and two s: one collar, two sleeves.
items.sentence: It is necessary to wear a helmet when you ride a bike.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
hints: Look at the last few letters for a clue.
Stationery with an e is the paper you write on.
Current and currant sound the same, but one is food.
items.explanation: Stationary with an a means still. Stationery with an e is paper goods. Currant is a fruit and current is a flow.

items.prompt: Listen and spell the word.
hints: Many people wrongly write per in the middle.
The middle of the word is par.
Sep, a, rate.
items.explanation: Separate has par in the middle: sep-a-rate. A common mistake is to write per.
items.sentence: Please keep the red pens separate from the blue ones.

items.prompt: Write the correct word. The school ___ welcomed the new pupils to the hall. (principal or principle)
hints: One of these words means the head of a school.
Principle means a rule or belief.
The principal is your pal.
items.explanation: The principal is the head of a school. A principle is a rule.

items.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? The heavy rain had a bad ___ on the match.
hints: After a bad, the sentence needs a naming word.
Effect with an e is a noun. Affect with an a is usually a verb.
Remember: a for action, e for the end result.
items.explanation: Effect is the noun for a result. Affect is usually the verb, as in The rain affected the match.

options.why: Affect is usually a verb. Here we need a noun after the word bad.
Affected is a verb form, so it cannot follow had a bad.
Affects is a verb form, so it cannot follow had a bad.

items.prompt: Everyone ___ Rangga was happy to ___ the invitation.
hints: Except means apart from.
Accept means to say yes to.
Try the sentence with apart from in the first gap.
items.explanation: Everyone except Rangga means everyone apart from Rangga. To accept an invitation is to say yes.

items.prompt: Sort the words by their ending.
hints: Look at the last four letters of each word.
Say the word, then picture its spelling.
Start with visible and possible.
items.explanation: These words have to be learned. Comfortable, adorable and valuable end in -able. Possible, terrible and visible end in -ible.

items.prompt: Which sentence has every word spelt correctly?
hints: Check each long word one at a time.
Receive follows the rule i before e except after c.
Look for the word finite inside definitely.
items.explanation: The correct spellings are definitely, received and pleasant.

options.text: I definately received a pleasant surprise.
options.why: Definitely has the word finite in the middle. It is not definate.

options.text: I definitely recieved a pleasant surprise.
options.why: Remember: i before e except after c. Receive has c before ei.

options.text: I definitely received a pleasant surprise.
I definitely received a plesant surprise.
options.why: Pleasant has an a after the s: pleas-ant.

items.prompt: One word is misspelt. Write it correctly. The new pupil felt embarassed on her first day.
hints: The wrong word is the long one.
It needs two of the same letter twice.
Embarrassed: two r and two s.
items.explanation: Embarrassed has double r and double s.

items.prompt: Listen and spell the word.
hints: It has no usual vowels a, e, i, o or u.
A memory trick: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move.
R-h-y-t-h-m.
items.explanation: Rhythm has no usual vowels. The letter y does the work.
items.sentence: The drummer kept a steady rhythm all through the song.

items.prompt: In which sentence does bear mean to put up with?
hints: Bear is a word with several meanings.
Replace bear with put up with and read it.
Which sentence is about a noise you do not like?
items.explanation: Bear can be an animal, to produce, or to put up with. Only the noise sentence means to put up with.

options.text: A bear woke up in the cave.
options.why: Here bear is an animal.

options.text: We saw a polar bear at the zoo.
options.why: Here bear is an animal.

options.text: The apple tree will bear fruit next year.
options.why: Here bear means to produce, not to put up with.

options.text: I cannot bear the noise of the drill.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that are spelt correctly.
hints: Check each word for double letters.
Accommodation has two c and two m.
Look at the word occasion.
items.explanation: Accommodation, embarrass and necessary are correct. The others have a letter wrong.

options.why: Occasion has only one s in the middle.
Necessary has only one c.
Separate has the word par in the middle.

items.prompt: Put the cards in order to make a correct sentence.
hints: The first word is a short form of two words.
Who’s means who is. Whose shows ownership.
Start with the capital letter.
items.explanation: Who’s means who is. Whose asks who something belongs to.
items.answer: Who’s the girl whose bag is red?

items.prompt: Which sentence uses practise and practice correctly in British English?
hints: One gap is an action. One is a thing.
Verbs use s, as with advise. Nouns use c, as with advice.
The first gap follows must.
items.explanation: Practise with an s is the verb and practice with a c is the noun in British English.

options.text: I must practice the piano before my practise starts.
options.why: In British English the verb is practise and the noun is practice.

options.text: I must practise the piano before my practise starts.
options.why: The thing that starts is a noun, so it needs the c spelling.

options.text: I must practise the piano before my practice starts.
I must practice the piano before my practice starts.
options.why: The first one is a verb, so it needs the s spelling.

items.prompt: Which sentence has every word spelt and chosen correctly?
hints: Every sentence looks nearly the same, so read slowly.
Check each pair: advice and advise, accept and except.
The first gap comes after the council’s.
items.explanation: Advice is a noun, accept means to agree to, and except means apart from.

options.text: The council’s advise was to accept the plan, except for the bridge.
options.why: Advise is the verb. The noun here is advice.

options.text: The council’s advice was to except the plan, except for the bridge.
options.why: Except means apart from. The council would accept, or agree to, the plan.

options.text: The council’s advice was to accept the plan, expect for the bridge.
options.why: Expect means to think something will happen. The word needed is except.

options.text: The council’s advice was to accept the plan, except for the bridge.

items.prompt: True or false: The word bank in "river bank" and the word bank in "bank account" are homonyms.
hints: Compare the spelling and sound of the two words.
Compare their meanings.
Same spelling, same sound, different meaning.
items.explanation: Homonyms are words with the same spelling and sound but different meanings.

items.prompt: True or false: In British English, practice is the correct spelling of the verb.
hints: Is the word in the sentence an action or a thing?
Think of licence and license.
The verb is spelt with an s.
items.explanation: In British English, practice is the noun and practise is the verb. We practise the piano.

items.prompt: True or false: In British English, the verb practise is spelt with an s.
hints: Decide whether you need a noun or a verb.
Verbs are action words.
The action word has an s.
items.explanation: The verb is practise and the noun is practice, as in I practise every day at football practice.

items.prompt: True or false: The words principal and principle mean the same.
hints: One of them can be a person.
Think of the principal of a school.
The other is a rule you live by.
items.explanation: A principal is the head of a school. A principle is a rule or belief.

items.prompt: True or false: The word affect is usually a verb and the word effect is usually a noun.
hints: Which spelling starts the action?
Affect is the action, effect is the result.
A is for action.
items.explanation: Rain can affect our plans, and the effect of the rain is wet clothes.

items.prompt: True or false: The words complement and compliment mean the same.
hints: One word has an e for enough, as in completing something.
A compliment is a kind thing to say.
Their meanings are different.
items.explanation: Complement means to go well with something. Compliment means a kind remark.

items.prompt: True or false: The word stationary means not moving.
hints: Think of a parked car that is not moving.
Stationery with an e is for envelopes.
Stationary with an a means still.
items.explanation: Stationary with an a means still. Stationery with an e means paper and pens.

items.prompt: Please ___ me what to do. (give advice)
hints: The verb ends in se.
The noun is advice.
a, d, v, i, s, e.
items.explanation: Advise is the verb. Advice is the noun.

items.prompt: Words spelt the same with different meanings are ___.
hints: A bat is an animal or a sports item.
They are not homophones.
It starts with homo.
items.explanation: Homonyms are words that look the same but have different meanings.
